items.author: Marilyn Manson

items.title: ActKV: Efficient LLM Agents through Action-Guided KV Cache Management
items.abstract: ActKV addresses the memory burden of LLM agents by prioritizing KV cache entries crucial for action generation. Its core method employs action-oriented eviction and confidence-driven budget allocation to retain relevant information, enabling more efficient and higher-throughput agentic inference. This contributes the first KV cache compression framework specifically designed to optimize agent performance by focusing on action quality.

items.title: DIAL: Position-Debiased LLM Judges with Adaptive Human Preference Calibration
items.abstract: DIAL addresses the limitations of LLM judges by developing a framework that combines LLM and human comparisons. It separates position biases in LLM judgments, learns their underlying preferences, and then adaptively calibrates these to align with human preferences. This approach offers a theoretically grounded and empirically robust method for more accurate LLM evaluation.
items.figure_caption: Overview of DIAL framework. (a) Pairwise evaluation combines abundant, scalable LLM judgments with limited, higher-fidelity human judgments. (b) Empirical examples illustrate two distinct challenges: position bias and human-preference misalignment. (c) DIAL jointly models LLM and human comparisons to separate judge-specific position effects from latent LLM preferences, learn shared preference structure across judges, and adaptively calibrate toward human preference.

items.title: Game Arena: Strategic LLM Evaluation in Competitive Environments
items.abstract: The paper introduces Kaggle Game Arena, a platform for evaluating LLMs through competitive gameplay. Its core method involves head-to-head matchups in structured game environments, allowing for dynamic performance assessment as models improve. The contribution lies in providing a robust, transparent, and reproducible system for studying LLM strategic capabilities across diverse game settings, overcoming the limitations of static benchmarks.

items.title: PriceBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Price, Quality, and Brand Preferences in LLM Booking Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces PriceBench, a benchmark designed to diagnose the price, quality, and brand preferences of Large Language Models (LLMs) acting as booking agents. By analyzing LLM booking choices using a logit model, the benchmark reveals that more capable LLMs exhibit stronger, more consistent preferences, while less capable ones are either overly biased or indifferent. The study highlights that these preferences vary significantly across different LLM providers and even within the same family, impacting what options are presented and at what cost.

items.title: Nonparametric In-Context Learning under Growing Geometric Complexity: Minimax Optimality and Local Geometry-Adaptivity of Transformers
items.abstract: This paper analyzes how Transformers perform in-context learning on data with complex, varying geometric structures. The core method involves developing a novel local-polynomial estimator that adapts to these heterogeneous manifolds. The key contribution is establishing minimax optimality for this type of learning, demonstrating that Transformers can effectively leverage local geometric information for prediction.
items.figure_caption: Schematic growing mixture geometry. Different pieces represent components with potentially different intrinsic dimensions and sampling masses; additional or closer pieces illustrate variation in K n K_{n} and δ 0 , n \( \delta_{0,n} \) . The point clouds indicate bounded covariate perturbations. Local chart regularity remains uniformly controlled, and the regression bandwidth stays below the reach and separation scales.

items.title: AgentXploit: Autonomous Repository-to-Runtime Red-Teaming for AI Agents
items.abstract: AgentXploit is an autonomous system for pre-deployment red-teaming of AI agents. It uses a two-agent approach: an Analyzer Agent discovers potential attack paths within the agent's code repository, and an Exploiter Agent translates these paths into concrete runtime attacks, refining them with feedback. This system's contribution is a novel, automated method for identifying and exploiting security vulnerabilities in AI agents before deployment, supported by a benchmark of 72 reproducible vulnerabilities.
items.figure_caption: Overview of AgentXploit. The Analyzer Agent searches the repository and records candidate attack paths with supporting code evidence. The evaluation harness launches an isolated target, and the Exploiter Agent tests those paths only through the attacker interface. An external deterministic verifier, rather than the agent, checks the specified security outcome.

items.title: Beyond Approved Actions: Runtime Validation of Persistent Outcomes in Agent Workflows
items.abstract: This paper introduces EffectMatch, a runtime validation system for LLM agents that interact with software. Its core method is to collect and compare persistent changes made by an agent's actions against the approved outcomes for the current state. EffectMatch's contribution is to prevent unapproved side effects from being accepted as success, thereby ensuring the integrity of agent workflows and preventing downstream errors.

items.title: Compact Documentation for Coding Agents: A Benchmark, an Optimizer, and Why It Does Not Transfer
items.abstract: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating code documentation by testing if regenerated code passes original tests, finding completeness, not length, is key. They developed an optimizer that creates highly faithful documentation, but surprisingly, this improved documentation did not help coding agents resolve real software issues, even when compared to using no documentation.
items.figure_caption: Roundtrip fidelity (mean ± \( \pm \) SD over three runs) against description density (tokens in the description over tokens in the code) across the eleven Verified fixtures.

items.title: DeepEdu-v1: Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs for Vietnamese Education
items.abstract: This paper introduces DeepEdu-v1, an AI tutoring system for Vietnamese education designed to address data sovereignty and curriculum alignment issues. Its core method, the SCALE framework, innovates by improving context-aware learning and self-improvement. This contributes a scalable, efficient agentic LLM that overcomes the limitations of existing solutions for localized educational AI.

items.title: Evaluating Cultural Awareness of LLMs for Haitian Creole
items.abstract: This paper introduces the first systematic evaluation of cultural awareness in LLMs for Haitian Creole. It uses a benchmark of culturally relevant prompts to assess specificity, bias, diversity, and variation, revealing significant gaps compared to French and highlighting issues like French linguistic interference and stereotypical portrayals of Haitian characters. The core contribution is establishing a methodology and dataset to identify and address cultural insensitivity in LLMs for underrepresented languages.
items.figure_caption: Examples of cultural entity infilling with ChatGPT and Mistral using contextualized cultural prompts. Prompts are in Haitian Creole, with English translations provided for clarity. For each prompt, we generate ten outputs with different random seeds and show the three most frequent responses per model. Responses highlighted in red are not aligned with the Haitian context.

items.title: Highlight-Then-Summarize: Learning to Compress Evidence for Long-Context Understanding
items.abstract: This paper introduces Highlight-Then-Summarize (H2S), a novel compress-then-reason approach for long-context understanding. H2S first identifies relevant evidence from lengthy documents and then generates a compact, question-conditioned summary of this evidence before producing the final answer. This method, trained with a new dataset and reinforcement learning, significantly improves performance on long-context tasks by effectively filtering and condensing information.
items.figure_caption: Highlight-Then-Summarize. H2S transforms a block-structured long document into source-addressable evidence and then a question-conditioned summary before producing the final answer in one autoregressive trajectory.

items.title: Multi-agent Scaling Across Disjunctive and Compensatory Tasks
items.abstract: This paper introduces Steiner's taxonomy of group tasks to analyze how multi-agent LLM performance scales with team size, focusing on disjunctive and compensatory tasks. The authors model agents as conditionally independent and derive theoretical limits for plurality voting and averaging. Their empirical findings show distinct scaling behaviors, with disjunctive tasks showing potential gains that plurality voting largely fails to capture, though multi-round revision improves accuracy.

items.title: Prompt Minimization: Reducing Input Redundancy Without Sacrificing Output Fidelity
items.abstract: This paper introduces "prompt minimization," a method to find the shortest possible prompts for large language models that still produce accurate outputs. By removing redundant information, their approach reduces computational costs and improves model performance. The core contribution is demonstrating that these minimal prompts can achieve comparable fidelity to longer, more verbose ones, highlighting the importance of efficient prompt design.

items.title: Statistical attribute alignment for black-box generative AI via output post-processing
items.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning generative AI outputs with user-specified attribute distributions in a black-box setting. The core method involves post-processing generated outputs to statistically match a target distribution for a specific attribute. The key contribution is the development of query-efficient algorithms that minimize the number of calls to the generative model, offering optimal solutions for achieving exact or approximate attribute alignment.
items.figure_caption: High-level illustration of statistical attribute alignment via black-box output post-processing, using demographic attributes of generated headshots as an example. A user queries a black-box generator to form an annotated candidate batch. A black-box post-processing method then filters the candidate batch by selecting outputs that match a user-specified target distribution (e.g., uniform) as closely as possible, subject to what was observed in the batch.

items.title: Towards Mitigating Fabricated Consensus: The Active Provenance Gate for Multi-Agent Debate Synthesis
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Active Provenance Gate (APG), a post-debate verification layer for multi-agent debate systems. The APG analyzes debate logs, audits claims, and self-corrects to prevent fabricated consensus, ensuring summaries are grounded in the debate's history. Its core contribution is a mechanism to enhance the reliability and factual accuracy of synthesized conclusions from LLM-based debates.

items.title: ViSTA: A Simple Bridge Extends Visual Alignment to Clinical Time-Series Understanding in Multimodal LLMs
items.abstract: ViSTA is a compact adapter that bridges clinical time-series data with multimodal large language models by learning corrections to visual tokens representing numerical measurements. This approach allows pretrained vision-language models to accurately predict clinical outcomes from structured patient data without altering their original parameters. ViSTA significantly improves prediction performance on benchmarks like MIMIC-IV, demonstrating its effectiveness in extending language model capabilities to clinical time-series understanding.
items.figure_caption: Numerical correction of an established visual interface. Direct numerical interfaces learn how to present a new continuous representation to a language model. Chart inputs use its pretrained visual pathway. ViSTA adds numerical corrections to original visual tokens at their existing positions, preserving token order and positional indices. The language model and its output head remain frozen.

items.title: New LoRA Skills Should Read but Never Write
items.abstract: This paper introduces READ, a method for combining multiple LoRA adapters without interference. READ rewrites each adapter into a canonical form that preserves its original update, allowing them to be merged into a single model. This approach avoids the issues of weight-space interference, expensive retraining, and complex routing, enabling efficient composition of specialized skills.

items.title: PIA: A Personal Intelligence Agent Turning Health Conversations into Records and Records into Understanding
items.abstract: PIA, a personal intelligence agent, addresses the limitations of general summarization for health data. Its core method involves a four-control memory harness (extraction, memory, retrieval, understanding) that converts health conversations into structured clinical records and then synthesizes these records into user understanding. PIA's contribution lies in its domain-agnostic memory mechanisms, enhanced by pluggable health modules, enabling more accurate and context-aware responses for health-related queries.

items.title: Stale-Document Poisoning: When Outdated Retrieval Overrides Correct Model Answers
items.abstract: This paper introduces "stale-document poisoning," a vulnerability in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) where outdated retrieved information causes models to provide incorrect answers, even if they would have been correct otherwise. The authors created a benchmark of knowledge reversals and demonstrated that outdated evidence significantly degrades model performance, particularly for recent factual changes. Their work highlights the critical need for temporal awareness in RAG systems to ensure the validity of retrieved information.
items.figure_caption: Retrieving outdated evidence can overturn an answer that the same model gets right without retrieval. The timely-answer margin changes little in early layers but drops sharply near the output. Even neutral retrieval causes substantial poisoning, and an explicit follow directive amplifies the effect. In contrast, matched up-to-date evidence is followed almost universally, revealing a failure of selective trust rather than a general failure to use retrieval.

items.title: Agentic Limit Order Books: Phase Transitions and Market Impact
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework of Limit Order Books populated solely by autonomous reinforcement-learning agents. The core method involves simulating agent interactions within an order-matching engine to study emergent market phenomena. The key contribution is the discovery of distinct phase transitions in trading regimes, from orderly price discovery to volatile cascades, and the identification of non-classical market impact dynamics driven by agent feedback loops.
items.figure_caption: Evolution of the Order Book in the Solid (left), Liquid (centre) and Vapour (right) Phases. Positive quantities denote Bids, negative quantities denote Asks, Mid Price is shown in black.

items.title: Ember-1
items.summary: Fireworks.ai has launched Ember-1, a powerful, open-source, 7-billion parameter LLM optimized for efficient inference and fine-tuning, aiming to democratize AI development.

items.title: There are no "rogue" AI agents
items.summary: The article argues that AI agents are not "rogue" but rather act according to their programming and data, with any perceived misbehavior stemming from design flaws or unexpected emergent properties.

items.title: As A.I. makes law firms more efficient, clients ask: 'Where's my discount?'
items.summary: As AI boosts law firm efficiency, clients are increasingly questioning why these cost savings aren't reflected in their bills, challenging the traditional billable hour model.

items.title: Show HN: TinyAIArena watch AI agents battle it out
items.summary: TinyAIArena showcases a platform where AI agents compete against each other in various challenges, allowing users to watch and potentially participate in these AI battles.

items.title: "As a Language Model": Chat Template Switches LLM Self-Referential Voice
items.summary: This paper explores how chat templates can alter a large language model's self-referential voice, impacting its perceived identity and how it describes itself.

items.description: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work
items.summary: Paperclip is an open-source application designed for managing AI agents at work, offering a centralized platform for their deployment and control.
Hindsight is an AI agent memory system that learns and adapts over time, enabling agents to recall and utilize past experiences to improve future decision-making and performance.

items.description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative — voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.
items.summary: VoiceStudio is an open-source, local ElevenLabs alternative enabling voice cloning, design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription, and audiobook creation across 646 languages.

items.description: Learn it. Build it. Ship it for others.
items.summary: This repository provides a hands-on guide to building and deploying AI systems from the ground up, emphasizing practical learning and application.

items.description: An open-source Android app to let you browse YouTube and other services freely.
items.summary: PipePipe is an open-source Android app designed for free browsing of YouTube and other services, offering a privacy-focused alternative to traditional platforms.
Scriptc is a TypeScript-to-Native compiler that allows you to write and compile TypeScript code into standalone native executables for various platforms.

items.description: Multi-agent harness that runs Claude Code and Codex together as one system
items.summary: Openrig is a multi-agent harness that integrates Claude Code and Codex to function as a single, cohesive system for code generation and execution.

items.description: The Office Harness for AI Agents — Spreadsheets, Docs, Slides, Canvas, Relational Tables, and PDF in one runtime.
items.summary: Univer is an office harness for AI agents, providing a unified runtime for interacting with spreadsheets, documents, slides, canvas, relational tables, and PDFs.

items.description: Run x86-64 Windows PC games on jailed iOS via FEX-Emu + Wine + DXMT
items.summary: This repository enables running x86-64 Windows PC games on jailed iOS devices by leveraging FEX-Emu for emulation, Wine for Windows compatibility, and DXMT for DirectX translation.

papers.abstract: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating code documentation by testing if regenerated code passes original tests, finding completeness, not length, is key. They developed an optimizer that creates highly faithful documentation, but surprisingly, this improved documentation did not help coding agents resolve real software issues, even when compared to using no documentation.
papers.figure_caption: Roundtrip fidelity (mean ± \( \pm \) SD over three runs) against description density (tokens in the description over tokens in the code) across the eleven Verified fixtures.

papers.title: DeepEdu-v1: Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs for Vietnamese Education
papers.abstract: This paper introduces DeepEdu-v1, an AI tutoring system for Vietnamese education designed to address data sovereignty and curriculum alignment issues. Its core method, the SCALE framework, innovates by improving context-aware learning and self-improvement. This contributes a scalable, efficient agentic LLM that overcomes the limitations of existing solutions for localized educational AI.

papers.title: Evaluating Cultural Awareness of LLMs for Haitian Creole
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the first systematic evaluation of cultural awareness in LLMs for Haitian Creole. It uses a benchmark of culturally relevant prompts to assess specificity, bias, diversity, and variation, revealing significant gaps compared to French and highlighting issues like French linguistic interference and stereotypical portrayals of Haitian characters. The core contribution is establishing a methodology and dataset to identify and address cultural insensitivity in LLMs for underrepresented languages.
papers.figure_caption: Examples of cultural entity infilling with ChatGPT and Mistral using contextualized cultural prompts. Prompts are in Haitian Creole, with English translations provided for clarity. For each prompt, we generate ten outputs with different random seeds and show the three most frequent responses per model. Responses highlighted in red are not aligned with the Haitian context.

papers.title: Highlight-Then-Summarize: Learning to Compress Evidence for Long-Context Understanding
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Highlight-Then-Summarize (H2S), a novel compress-then-reason approach for long-context understanding. H2S first identifies relevant evidence from lengthy documents and then generates a compact, question-conditioned summary of this evidence before producing the final answer. This method, trained with a new dataset and reinforcement learning, significantly improves performance on long-context tasks by effectively filtering and condensing information.
papers.figure_caption: Highlight-Then-Summarize. H2S transforms a block-structured long document into source-addressable evidence and then a question-conditioned summary before producing the final answer in one autoregressive trajectory.

papers.title: Multi-agent Scaling Across Disjunctive and Compensatory Tasks
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Steiner's taxonomy of group tasks to analyze how multi-agent LLM performance scales with team size, focusing on disjunctive and compensatory tasks. The authors model agents as conditionally independent and derive theoretical limits for plurality voting and averaging. Their empirical findings show distinct scaling behaviors, with disjunctive tasks showing potential gains that plurality voting largely fails to capture, though multi-round revision improves accuracy.

papers.title: Prompt Minimization: Reducing Input Redundancy Without Sacrificing Output Fidelity
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "prompt minimization," a method to find the shortest possible prompts for large language models that still produce accurate outputs. By removing redundant information, their approach reduces computational costs and improves model performance. The core contribution is demonstrating that these minimal prompts can achieve comparable fidelity to longer, more verbose ones, highlighting the importance of efficient prompt design.

papers.title: Statistical attribute alignment for black-box generative AI via output post-processing
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning generative AI outputs with user-specified attribute distributions in a black-box setting. The core method involves post-processing generated outputs to statistically match a target distribution for a specific attribute. The key contribution is the development of query-efficient algorithms that minimize the number of calls to the generative model, offering optimal solutions for achieving exact or approximate attribute alignment.
papers.figure_caption: High-level illustration of statistical attribute alignment via black-box output post-processing, using demographic attributes of generated headshots as an example. A user queries a black-box generator to form an annotated candidate batch. A black-box post-processing method then filters the candidate batch by selecting outputs that match a user-specified target distribution (e.g., uniform) as closely as possible, subject to what was observed in the batch.

papers.title: Towards Mitigating Fabricated Consensus: The Active Provenance Gate for Multi-Agent Debate Synthesis
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Active Provenance Gate (APG), a post-debate verification layer for multi-agent debate systems. The APG analyzes debate logs, audits claims, and self-corrects to prevent fabricated consensus, ensuring summaries are grounded in the debate's history. Its core contribution is a mechanism to enhance the reliability and factual accuracy of synthesized conclusions from LLM-based debates.

papers.title: ViSTA: A Simple Bridge Extends Visual Alignment to Clinical Time-Series Understanding in Multimodal LLMs
papers.abstract: ViSTA is a compact adapter that bridges clinical time-series data with multimodal large language models by learning corrections to visual tokens representing numerical measurements. This approach allows pretrained vision-language models to accurately predict clinical outcomes from structured patient data without altering their original parameters. ViSTA significantly improves prediction performance on benchmarks like MIMIC-IV, demonstrating its effectiveness in extending language model capabilities to clinical time-series understanding.
papers.figure_caption: Numerical correction of an established visual interface. Direct numerical interfaces learn how to present a new continuous representation to a language model. Chart inputs use its pretrained visual pathway. ViSTA adds numerical corrections to original visual tokens at their existing positions, preserving token order and positional indices. The language model and its output head remain frozen.

papers.title: New LoRA Skills Should Read but Never Write
papers.abstract: This paper introduces READ, a method for combining multiple LoRA adapters without interference. READ rewrites each adapter into a canonical form that preserves its original update, allowing them to be merged into a single model. This approach avoids the issues of weight-space interference, expensive retraining, and complex routing, enabling efficient composition of specialized skills.

papers.title: PIA: A Personal Intelligence Agent Turning Health Conversations into Records and Records into Understanding
papers.abstract: PIA, a personal intelligence agent, addresses the limitations of general summarization for health data. Its core method involves a four-control memory harness (extraction, memory, retrieval, understanding) that converts health conversations into structured clinical records and then synthesizes these records into user understanding. PIA's contribution lies in its domain-agnostic memory mechanisms, enhanced by pluggable health modules, enabling more accurate and context-aware responses for health-related queries.

papers.title: Stale-Document Poisoning: When Outdated Retrieval Overrides Correct Model Answers
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "stale-document poisoning," a vulnerability in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) where outdated retrieved information causes models to provide incorrect answers, even if they would have been correct otherwise. The authors created a benchmark of knowledge reversals and demonstrated that outdated evidence significantly degrades model performance, particularly for recent factual changes. Their work highlights the critical need for temporal awareness in RAG systems to ensure the validity of retrieved information.
papers.figure_caption: Retrieving outdated evidence can overturn an answer that the same model gets right without retrieval. The timely-answer margin changes little in early layers but drops sharply near the output. Even neutral retrieval causes substantial poisoning, and an explicit follow directive amplifies the effect. In contrast, matched up-to-date evidence is followed almost universally, revealing a failure of selective trust rather than a general failure to use retrieval.

papers.title: Agentic Limit Order Books: Phase Transitions and Market Impact
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework of Limit Order Books populated solely by autonomous reinforcement-learning agents. The core method involves simulating agent interactions within an order-matching engine to study emergent market phenomena. The key contribution is the discovery of distinct phase transitions in trading regimes, from orderly price discovery to volatile cascades, and the identification of non-classical market impact dynamics driven by agent feedback loops.
papers.figure_caption: Evolution of the Order Book in the Solid (left), Liquid (centre) and Vapour (right) Phases. Positive quantities denote Bids, negative quantities denote Asks, Mid Price is shown in black.
